## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest)

## Description

This epic defines the tutorial packaging format that makes tutorials versioned
and testable independently of Dashboard releases. It produces the format
specification — tutorial metadata, pinned images, and a validation manifest —
plus the means to validate a packaged tutorial against that manifest. The
format is the shared artifact that the Dashboard tutorial gallery renders and
launches, and that every curated tutorial is authored, packaged, and tested
against.

## Scope

- Define the tutorial metadata model a packaged tutorial carries (identity,
  journey description, launch hints for both a workbench notebook and an
  imported pipeline).
- Define the pinned-image policy for tutorial content so a tutorial always
  runs against known image versions.
- Define the validation manifest and the validation pass that checks a
  packaged tutorial for completeness and correctness without requiring a
  Dashboard release.
- Define versioning rules so a tutorial can be updated and re-tested
  independently of Dashboard release cadence.
- Document the format for the teams that author tutorials and build the
  gallery.

The scope stays at the format level: concrete schema field names, storage
location, and tooling implementation choices are decisions for the
implementing team.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A format specification exists covering tutorial metadata, image pinning,
  and the validation manifest, with versioning rules that allow a tutorial to
  be updated without a Dashboard release.
- A tutorial packaged according to the format passes the format's validation
  pass (manifest checks complete and pass) without any Dashboard release
  being involved.
- The format is reviewed and agreed by the teams that consume it: the
  Dashboard gallery implementers and the tutorial authors for both notebook
  and pipeline tutorials.
- Packaging an example tutorial per the format is demonstrated end to end
  (metadata present, images pinned, validation manifest passes).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)**: "A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images,
  validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable
  independently of Dashboard releases." This epic is the direct
  implementation of HLR-3. Note: the epic's priority is P0 by priority
  inheritance — the packaging format is the prerequisite artifact that the P0
  gallery and P0 tutorial work build against, while the HLR itself is
  labeled P1 in the strategy.

# Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch into projects

## Description

This epic delivers the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: a curated, surfaced
set of tutorials that a user can launch into their own project with one click.
Launching a notebook tutorial opens a workbench in the user's project with the
tutorial notebook loaded; launching a pipeline tutorial imports the pipeline
into the user's project. The gallery renders packaged tutorials from their
metadata and launch hints.

## Scope

- Add the tutorial gallery surface to the Dashboard (navigation entry and the
  gallery view listing curated tutorials from their packaged metadata).
- Implement one-click launch of a notebook tutorial: create/open a workbench
  in the user's project with the tutorial notebook available in it.
- Implement one-click launch of a pipeline tutorial: import the pipeline into
  the user's project through the platform's pipeline interface.
- Consume the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation
  manifest) so tutorials are rendered and launched from their packages,
  versioned independently of Dashboard releases.
- Gate the gallery through the Dashboard's existing per-component feature
  configuration so it can be enabled/disabled without code changes.
- Fold in any captions, labels, or reference updates in the Dashboard that
  fall out of this change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can open the tutorial gallery from the Dashboard and see the curated
  tutorials with their metadata.
- Launching a notebook tutorial from the gallery opens a workbench in the
  user's project with the tutorial notebook loaded, using the tutorial's
  pinned images.
- Launching a pipeline tutorial from the gallery imports the pipeline into
  the user's project and the imported pipeline is visible in the project's
  pipeline view (this validates the Data Science Pipelines integration — no
  pipeline platform code changes are in scope for this epic).
- End-to-end launch of at least one packaged tutorial of each kind (workbench
  notebook and imported pipeline) is verified against the current release.
- The gallery can be disabled through the Dashboard's existing configuration
  mechanism.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: "The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can
  launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the
  notebook, or importing the pipeline)." This epic is the direct
  implementation of HLR-1, covering both launch modes.

# Curated notebook tutorials for five core onboarding journeys

## Description

This epic authors five of the six curated tutorials as notebook-based
content, covering the core onboarding journeys: first workbench, data prep,
first training run, first deployment, and first RAG app. Each tutorial is
packaged according to the tutorial packaging format, pinned to known images,
and tested against the current release so a new user can go from a blank
project to a first success by following it.

## Scope

- Author the five notebook tutorials:
  1. First workbench — creating a project and a first workbench.
  2. Data prep — loading and preparing data in a workbench.
  3. First training run — training a first model.
  4. First deployment — deploying a first model.
  5. First RAG app — building a first retrieval-augmented generation app.
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
  images, validation manifest).
- Test each tutorial against the current release and record the result.
- Keep the five tutorials consistent as one curated set (shared style,
  progression, and packaging).

The first-pipeline tutorial (the sixth journey) is authored separately by the
pipelines team; this epic covers the five notebook-centric journeys.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Five notebook tutorials exist covering the named journeys: first workbench,
  data prep, first training run, first deployment, and first RAG app.
- Each tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format and passes the
  format's validation manifest.
- Each tutorial has a recorded successful test run against the current
  release.
- Each tutorial pins its images so it runs against known image versions.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: "Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys:
  first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first
  deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release."
  This epic covers five of the six journeys (the notebook-centric ones); the
  first-pipeline journey is covered by the pipelines-team tutorial epic.

# Tutorial gallery usage and contribution documentation

## Description

This epic documents the tutorial gallery for two audiences: end users who
launch tutorials from the gallery, and contributors who want to add new
tutorials. It covers using the gallery and the contribution process defined
by the tutorial packaging format, and it is authored through the Red Hat
docs content process after the implemented work it describes.

## Scope

Content outline:

- **Using the tutorial gallery** (user-facing topic): what the gallery is,
  how to open it, how to launch a notebook tutorial into a workbench, and
  how to launch a pipeline tutorial into a project.
- **Contributing a new tutorial** (contribution process): the tutorial
  packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest), the
  validation and testing requirements a tutorial must pass, and how a
  tutorial gets added to the curated set.

Out of scope, mirroring the strategy: partner- or community-contributed
tutorial intake tooling (the process is documented, but no submission
tooling this release) and localization of tutorial content.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers using the gallery: opening it and launching
  both kinds of tutorial (workbench notebook and imported pipeline).
- Published documentation describes the contribution process for new
  tutorials, including the packaging format and the validation/testing
  requirements.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery
  and tutorials and any discrepancies found in review are fixed.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: "Documentation covers using the gallery and the
  contribution process for new tutorials." This epic is the direct
  implementation of HLR-4. Note: the epic's priority is P1 per the
  docs-authoring priority exception, derived from the strategy's overall
  priority (Major), not from the HLR's P2 label.
